WikiOasisSafetyEnabled.description: Master switch for the "get help or report a problem" entry points.

WikiOasisSafetyNoticeboard.description: Page the guidance cards link to. Any card in the wizard definition without its own url links here.

WikiOasisSafetyWizard.description: Wizard-level wording and behaviour: title, description, submitLabel, nextLabel, backLabel. Each may instead be named as a message with a `-message` twin -- `title-message` -- which is what makes a flow translatable; see includes/Wording.php. Left unset entirely, the wizard falls back to wikioasissafety-title, -next, -back and -submit, which the extension already ships translated, so a flow only needs to set these when it has something else to say.

WikiOasisSafetySteps.description: The wizard itself: step definitions keyed by step id, in the order they are offered. The extension ships no steps; with none configured no entry points are offered. Any key carrying text -- a step title or description, a field label, helpText, placeholder or defaultLabel, an option label, a card's text -- has a `-message` twin naming a message instead, and the twin wins over a literal beside it; that is how a flow is translated, since the client cannot declare message keys a wiki has not written yet. See includes/Wording.php, and tests/php/ExampleConfiguration.php for a complete flow.

WikiOasisSafetyExclusiveFields.description: Groups of field names that are alternatives to each other: answering one forgets the others, follow-up text included.

WikiOasisSafetyFieldRoles.description: Which field a prefilled report writes into, keyed by role: concerns, pages, users, wikis, details. A role left out is not prefilled.

WikiOasisSafetyDataWizard.description: Wizard-level wording and behaviour for the manage-my-data flow: title, description, submitLabel, nextLabel, backLabel.

WikiOasisSafetyDataSteps.description: The manage-my-data flow, offered by the "Manage my data" card on Special:SafetyHome: step definitions keyed by step id, in the order they are offered. With none configured the card says the route is not available here. See tests/php/ExampleConfiguration.php.

WikiOasisSafetyContactWizard.description: Wizard-level wording and behaviour for the contact Trust & Safety flow: title, description, submitLabel, nextLabel, backLabel.

WikiOasisSafetyContactSteps.description: The contact Trust & Safety flow, offered by the "Contact Trust & Safety" card on Special:SafetyHome: step definitions keyed by step id, in the order they are offered. With none configured the card says the route is not available here. See tests/php/ExampleConfiguration.php.

WikiOasisSafetyContactExclusiveFields.description: As $wgWikiOasisSafetyExclusiveFields, for the contact Trust & Safety flow.

WikiOasisSafetyContactFieldRoles.description: As $wgWikiOasisSafetyFieldRoles, for the contact Trust & Safety flow.

WikiOasisSafetyCategories.description: The vocabulary the report flow's answers are categorised into: { id: { label, group, description } }, or { id: label } when there is nothing to say beyond the wording. A label may be named as a message with `label-message` instead, which a transparency report published in more than one language needs. An option in $wgWikiOasisSafetySteps carries `category` to name one; an option whose own `value` is a category id needs no `category` key, which is what lets an existing flow start categorising without every option being edited. Resolved on the server — see includes/Categories.php — because these are counted into published transparency reports and a figure in one must not be something a browser could have been talked into sending. With none declared, submissions are uncategorised, which the portal treats as "somebody has to read this" rather than guessing.

WikiOasisSafetyContactCategories.description: As $wgWikiOasisSafetyCategories, for the contact Trust & Safety flow. Worth setting separately: a message to Trust & Safety is about a policy question or a press enquiry, not about harassment or copyright, and one list holding both offers every reader categories that cannot apply to what they are writing.

WikiOasisSafetyCheckUserTracking.description: Send Trust & Safety the metadata of CheckUser checks run on this wiki: who ran each check, the reason they gave, what kind of target, and when. Never what a check returned. Off by default and deliberately so — shipping a wiki's CheckUser log somewhere new is a decision for the people who granted the right, not a side effect of an extension upgrade. Nothing needs scheduling: a check is sent to the portal after the response that ran it has gone out, and queues in wos_outbox if the portal is unreachable.

WikiOasisSafetyCheckUserTargets.description: How much of a check's target leaves the wiki. `accounts` (the default) sends an account name as itself and reduces an IP or range to a keyed fingerprint, so the portal can count repeat checks against one target without ever holding the address. `all` sends every target as it was typed, IPs included — only for a portal held to the same standard as the wiki. `none` sends no target at all: who, why, when and what kind, and nothing more. An unrecognised value falls back to `accounts`, because a typo here must not be the reason a farm starts shipping IP addresses.

WikiOasisSafetyCheckUserBatch.description: How many checks may be sent in one request. A ceiling rather than a target — an ordinary check sends one row — and bounded to 1000, which is what the portal accepts at once.

WikiOasisSafetyPortalUrl.description: Base URL of TSPortal, with no trailing slash. Empty means no portal: submissions cannot be sent and the wizard says so rather than pretending.

WikiOasisSafetyPortalSecret.description: Shared secret for signing requests to and from TSPortal. Generate it with the portal's `php artisan tsportal:secret`. Anyone holding it can file reports and read any account's standing; treat it as a password.

WikiOasisSafetyPortalTimeout.description: Seconds to wait for the portal. Kept short: a reporter is watching, and a queued submission that is delivered a minute later is better than a page that hangs.

WikiOasisSafetyPortalTolerance.description: How far apart this wiki's clock and the portal's may be, in seconds, before a signed request is refused.

WikiOasisSafetyMaxUploadSize.description: Largest attachment, in bytes, that this wiki will forward to the portal. The portal is the authority on the real limit and refuses again at its end (TS_ATTACHMENTS_MAX_BYTES there); this exists so a wiki does not read a 400 MB file into memory in order to be told it was too big, which is a thing one reporter could otherwise use to exhaust it. Keep it at or below the portal's, and below PHP's own upload_max_filesize and post_max_size, which refuse earlier still and with a much worse message. 0 disables the wiki's own check and leaves it entirely to the portal. Default 25 MB.

WikiOasisSafetyPiiDeletions.description: Extra rows to delete when erasing an account, keyed by table: { table: [ { where: { column: value } } ] }. Merged over the built-in list in includes/Pii/PiiTables.php, so adding an operation to a table already covered keeps both. Set a table to an empty list to stop the built-in one. Use this for rows that exist only to record personal data; anything that has to survive for another reason belongs in $wgWikiOasisSafetyPiiUpdates instead.

WikiOasisSafetyPiiUpdates.description: Extra rows to blank rather than delete when erasing an account, keyed by table: { table: [ { fields: { column: value }, where: { column: value } } ] }. For rows that have to survive — a recent-changes entry is the record of an edit — and merely carry personal data along with them.

WikiOasisSafetyPiiNamespaces.description: Extra namespace numbers holding an account's own pages, deleted with suppression when it is erased. User, user talk and the social-profile namespaces are covered already when their extensions are loaded.
